rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's twenty-one builder trees go (corals, ficus, three fan palms 3-4 m from the house fronts, a canary date palm, magnolias and jacarandas); five come back on their own spots, about one for every two or three houses: by the patio set, the grill, the arbor, an adirondack chair, and on the open lot corner.

trees.why: the back yard with the white adirondack and the patio set: a magnolia over the table
the west back yard with the garden arbor (2.5 m off): a jacaranda beside it
the south-west yard with the kettle grill (1.7 m off): a magnolia over the cook
the south-east yard's adirondack chair (1.7 m off): a coral tree to sit under
the open lot corner at the south-west, 25 m from the walls: a full coral tree
